# Ruby Gillis

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventeen at the time of her death  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018), [v3 c11 P0](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Ruby Gillis was handsome and bright, with a plump, showy figure, a brilliant complexion, large blue eyes, and long, thick golden-yellow hair. As her illness progressed, she became very thin and pale with hectically brilliant cheeks, though she retained her beauty until her death.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v3 c11 P0](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0000), [v3 c11 P1](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0001), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005), [v3 c14 P31](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0031)_

## Personality

Ruby was cheerful, good-tempered, and loved the pleasant things of life, though she was naturally vain, sentimental, and obsessed with boys and romance from a young age. She enjoyed flirtation and constantly talked about her admirers and compliments. Despite her shallow interests, she was fond of children and cared deeply for her schoolmates. Facing a fatal illness, she fought desperately for life and confessed her dread of death and the unknown before finding peace at the end.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P5](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0005), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P23](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0023)_

## History

Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school alongside Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. After completing her studies at Queen's Academy, she earned a teacher's license and took a teaching position at Carmody School. Known for her beauty and flirtatious nature, she pursued a lively social life surrounded by suitors. However, after contracting a severe lung congestion, she developed galloping consumption and was forced to give up teaching. Throughout her illness, Ruby maintained a facade of recovery and spoke constantly of her future plans, but privately suffered great dread of dying young. Shortly before her death, she reconciled an old feud with her childhood friend Emma White and confessed her fears and heartaches to Anne. Ruby passed away peacefully in her sleep at the age of seventeen, leaving a lasting impression of her beauty upon the Avonlea community.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P8](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0008), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v2 c26 P58](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0058), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P23](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0023), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c14 P31](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0031)_

> I don't care a single bit about either of them, you know. Herb Spencer is the one I like. Sometimes I really do think he's Mr. Right.  <sub>[v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053)</sub>

> I'm not afraid but that I'll go to heaven, Anne. I'm a church member. But—it'll be all so different. I think—and think—and I get so frightened—and—and—homesick.  <sub>[v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)</sub>
